jobs.title: [PMO-NSCS] Assistant Director (Policy 3)
jobs.jd: Posting Date: 14 Aug 2026. Closing on 28 Aug 2026. The National Security Coordination Secretariat (NSCS) is a unit under the Prime Minister's Office responsible for national security planning and coordination. NSCS works with agencies and stakeholders to develop and co-ordinate strategies to address national security concerns. NSCS also works with agencies to anticipate and identify emergent security risks, and to build up capabilities and resources to deal with these. The role will give you the opportunity to strengthen: • Critical Thinking: You will lead your team to keep abreast of national security developments and synthesise information across domains (geopolitical, economic, social, environment, information, etc.) to identify and analyse cross-cutting national security risks. These include economic security risks, digital security risks, concentration risks, and inter-dependency risks. • Systems Thinking: You will lead your team to integrate analysis of external developments with assessments of Singapore’s vulnerabilities and how the latter will change over time. You will recommend the best way to structure the Whole-of-Government response to the risk. This will require you to suggest constructive solutions which balance multiple policy considerations across domains. For specific risks, you could contribute to the full policy value-chain from strategic planning, policy formulation, policy-operations, to comms and implementation (e.g., legislation). • Influence: You will need to mobilise colleagues from a wide range of agencies, with different mandates and policy considerations, to work with you on the overall risk assessment. You will need to build consensus on the risk level Singapore can live with and the Whole-of-Government action needed to mitigate the risks. This would require you to build extensive and deep networks across domains and seniority levels, and develop a deep understanding of their considerations and constraints. You will work in a team: • To hunt out Singapore’s cross-cutting vulnerabilities (e.g., in critical infrastructure, social resilience) that could be exploited/ disrupted and build shared risk pictures (through data analysis and/ or policy analysis) to inform decision-making by public sector leaders. • To mobilise collective Whole-of-Government efforts to tackle complex, collective-action problems. This could involve putting forth recommendations which could sub-optimise agency-specific objectives to achieve better national outcomes. Depending on your performance and experience, you could be given the opportunity to lead a team or project. • At least five years of policy experience preferred; • Intellectual curiosity, and clear logical and systems thinking; • Excellent writing skills to deliver analyses synthesising information from multiple domains, including data-driven outputs; • Experience engaging multiple agencies and stakeholders, with skills to listen empathetically, sense dynamics, and persuade and negotiate across agencies and seniority levels to achieve desired outcomes; • Ability to move between macro and micro perspectives; • Preferably an intuitive grasp of Singapore’s security imperatives; • Interest in current affairs; • Ability to work in a dynamic environment and pick up new skills/ domain knowledge if necessary; and • Proactive, articulate, purpose-driven, persistent . We may refer you as a potential candidate for vacancies in other agencies we assessed you to be suitable for. By applying for this job, you are aware of, and are also giving NSCS consent for the cross referral. If you do not wish to be cross referred, please inform us via this link: https://go.gov.sg/candidateoptout.

MTI’s Energy Markets and Infrastructure Division plays a key role in ensuring Singapore’s energy security and creating an energy system that is resilient, cost-competitive, and ready to transition to a low carbon future. Energy security is an existential issue for Singapore. We import almost all our energy supply and are exposed to global energy market movements. The energy crisis after COVID and the war in Ukraine have upended the global energy ecosystem. The climate crisis compels all countries to accelerate their pace of decarbonisation, even as they struggle with energy costs and unpredictable supply chain shocks. Amidst this backdrop, Singapore needs a stable, reliable, and cost competitive energy system that keeps the lights on and safeguards our economic competitiveness and dynamism. MTI’s Energy and Carbon (E&C) Cluster leads initiatives to reduce emissions and drive the transition to a low-carbon economy, while ensuring energy security and cost-competitiveness, and enabling Singapore to sustain economic growth. Officers in this cluster develop energy and carbon markets, plan energy infrastructure, build Singapore’s capabilities to harness low-carbon energy sources, and manage emission trajectories and carbon budgets. You will collaborate with stakeholders across Government, industry, and international partners to support sustainable economic transformation and green growth through strategic planning, policy analysis, and partnerships. The Energy Markets and Infrastructure Division within the E&C Cluster takes the lead in: • Planning for Singapore’s energy transition and resilience, including energy demand and supply and the corresponding impact on infrastructure requirements, system costs and electricity prices. • Strengthening Singapore’s gas and electricity markets and our national grid infrastructure • Developing horizontal enablers for the energy sector e.g. manpower and skills development, energy public engagement strategy. Your responsibilities include one or more of the following workstreams: • Formulate robust strategies and policies to regulate and develop the gas and electricity sectors. This involves working with key stakeholders to develop and implement regulatory and market structures, to strike a balance among our objectives of economic competitiveness, energy security and environmental sustainability. • Formulate and review strategies and policies to enhance our energy security by diversifying Singapore’s energy sources, including those for electricity and gas imports. • Formulate and review policies and strategies to develop supporting enablers for the electricity and gas sectors, including infrastructure and financing. • Develop and implement communications and engagement plans to support electricity and gas market changes. • Monitor developments in global energy markets and analyse implications for domestic energy policies. jobs.title: Senior/Assistant Director, Trade Strategy & Security Division
jobs.jd: Posting Date: 15 May 2026. We are seeking a skilled and motivated individual to join our team as an Assistant/Senior Assistant Director in the Trade Strategy and Security Division in MTI. In this role, you will help develop policies and strategies to advance and safeguard Singapore’s economic and security interests in the international arena. You will also be MTI’s counterparty to other Government agencies and key committees that cover the range of geo-political and security spheres. As a TIER officer in the Trade Strategy and Security Division, you will be part of a dynamic team working on fast-moving pieces to help Singapore navigate changes in our geo-economic environment. You will have the opportunity to hone your strategic thinking skillset, policy acumen, and international orientation perspectives in both the economic and security domains, by: • Assessing the impact and implications of geo-political developments on Singapore’s economic and security interests; • Developing strategies, policies, options and responses to expand Singapore’s economic heft or relevance as well as strengthen Singapore’s economic resilience; • Preparing and executing communications and engagement strategies with key public and private sector stakeholders; • Organising and representing MTI at various high-level inter-agency platforms related to economic, security, and geo-political portfolios; and • Collaborating and networking with various internal and external stakeholders. jobs.title: Senior/Assistant Director, International Trade (GES)
jobs.jd: Posting Date: 15 May 2026. The Trade and International Economic Relations (TIER) cluster drives the formulation of Singapore's foreign economic policy and advances Singapore's economic interests in the international economic arena. Climate change is one of the defining issues of our time. It is a complex global challenge that calls for concerted international action and collaboration between governments, industry and individuals. As a low-lying city state, Singapore is particularly vulnerable to the effects of climate change and has a strong interest in shaping effective global climate action. The Green Economy and Sustainability (GES) team sits within MTI’s International Trade Division, which is charged with formulating Singapore’s foreign economic policy and advancing Singapore’s economic interests in the internationally. The GES team leads Singapore’s international economic engagement on green trade issues. We also work closely with agencies, such as MSE, MOF, NEA and PMO(NCCS), to formulate and coordinate strategies to chart the path forward for Singapore’s transition to a low-carbon economy. As a TIER officer in the International Trade (GES) Division in the Ministry of Trade and Industry, you will be part of a high-performing team operating at the forefront of international economic diplomacy and climate policy, shaping the rules and frameworks that will define the global green economy. You will work on one or more of the following work streams: a. Negotiation of Article 6.2 bilateral/plurilateral agreements. Develop and implement strategies and policies to strengthen bilateral cooperation with like-minded countries on carbon credits aligned with Article 6 of the Paris Agreement. Officer will negotiate binding bilateral and plurilateral agreements with foreign governments, drive technical cooperation initiatives, and build robust project development pipelines — directly contributing to Singapore's ability to meet its Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC). b. Global carbon market rules and standards setting. Monitor and analyse evolving global carbon market developments and develop strategies to actively shape the international rules and standards that govern high-integrity carbon markets, positioning Singapore as a credible and influential voice in this space. c. Green trade policy development. Synthesise geopolitical, trade, and climate trends to craft Singapore's green trade policy agenda, safeguarding the country's long-term economic competitiveness through the low-carbon transition. The officer’s work will directly inform how Singapore positions itself in an increasingly climate-conscious global trading environment. d. Green trade instruments negotiation. Negotiate international instruments across multilateral, plurilateral, and bilateral fronts to advance Singapore's green trade interests. Officer will work with Ministries across the government to tackle complex, cross-cutting issues spanning environmental goods, services and investments, trade-related climate measures (TrCMs), environmental attribute certificates (EACs), and sectoral areas such as sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) and green buildings. e. Multilateral negotiations. Represent Singapore at the highest levels of international climate diplomacy, including at the UNFCCC Conference of the Parties (COP). You will advocate for Singapore's green economy and low-carbon interests, building coalitions and influencing outcomes that have real-world consequences for global climate action. As the climate space is fast evolving, an officer may be deployed across different workstreams, based on the officer’s development and MTI’s organisational needs. • Experience in cross-cultural negotiations and international relations, particularly in the public sector; and/or • Good knowledge in carbon credits/markets and Paris Agreement; and/or • Good knowledge of green trade related issues including trade-related climate measures, environmental attributes certifications and se

jobs.title: Senior/Assistant Director, ASEAN Division
jobs.jd: Posting Date: 15 May 2026. The Trade and International Economic Relations (TIER) cluster drives the formulation of Singapore's foreign economic policy and advances Singapore's economic interests in the international economic arena. ASEAN – Where Proximity, Policies, Partners, and People Intersect Position Overview: Trade Negotiator and Economic Policy Officer Proximity: As we prepare for the future economy, the ASEAN region offers exciting growth opportunities. To enable our businesses and jobholders to seize these opportunities, MTI’s ASEAN Division advances Singapore’s economic interests and deepens regional economic integration at the ASEAN platform. Specifically, we seek to boost flows of goods, services, investments, data, people and ideas to strengthen the broader regional economic ecosystem. Policies: Our team negotiates/reviews regional Agreements at the ASEAN platform to lower tariffs, address non-tariff barriers, improve trade facilitation, grow services flows, enhance the digital ecosystem, and address sustainability challenges amongst others, to improve the ease of doing business and harness the potential of emerging opportunities. Beyond Free Trade Agreements (FTAs), we also develop new initiatives and forms of cooperation to expand economic space through engagement, capacity building, and collaboration. Partners: We nurture and work with partners to drive and champion deepening economic integration through the ASEAN Economic Community (AEC), a key trading partner and investment destination for Singapore. Beyond the 10 ASEAN Member States, the AEC provides opportunities for Singapore-based businesses to take advantage of ASEAN’s Agreements and initiatives with various external partners to facilitate their exports, investments and business activities. ASEAN’s suite of partners includes Australia, Canada, China, the European Union, India, Hong Kong, Japan, Korea, New Zealand, and the United States, amongst others. To ensure businesses can benefit, we also engage stakeholders such as business councils and research institutions to increase awareness and understanding. People: Our team invests in building human capital. We have a unique opportunity to represent Singapore at Free Trade Agreement negotiations, analyse key developments and their potential implications, and take ownership for driving meaningful outcomes. Trade officers in MTI’s ASEAN Division develop technical competencies in either the domain of goods or the domain of digital economy, services, and investment. They gain experience in negotiations, public policy writing, and strategy development, including developing ideas to advance integration under the AEC and how Singapore should engage ASEAN on the economic track amidst a challenging global economic environment. As trade diplomats, we also sharpen skills such as coalition building and relationship management with counterparts in the region and beyond. • Keen interest in international economic affairs and negotiations; • Strong analytical and conceptual abilities, with an eye for detail; • Excellent written and oral communication skills; • Self-starter, versatile and adaptable to different environments; • Ability to work well in teams and engage people; • Ability to work in a fast-paced and dynamic environment; and • Willingness to travel frequently

jobs.jd: Posting Date: 9 Jun 2026. Closing on 31 Aug 2026. Oversee and provide advice on conservation work undertaken by conservators in the Inorganic Objects section, including collections care, conservation treatments, scientific analyses, and project management. Ensure that conservation guidelines and standards of practice for a holistic approach to collections care and access are based on current ethics and principles, and that they are timely and adequately implemented by the section within allocated resources. About ACRA The Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority (ACRA) is the national regulator of business entities, public accountants, and corporate service providers in Singapore. ACRA's mission is to foster a vibrant and trusted business environment that enables innovation and growth. As ACRA embarks on a significant digital transformation journey — shifting from a project-based to a product-led organisation, the IT Division plays a central role in delivering on ACRA's corporate goals and strategic outcomes. [What you will be working on] As a Deputy Director, Programme Management, you are an experienced leader who will be responsible for overseeing ACRA's digital transformation programme. You will work closely with the CIO and senior leadership to deliver on ACRA's mission, corporate goals, and strategic IT direction — spanning transformation initiatives, product development, and day-to-day digital operations. At this level, you will be expected to identify strategic opportunities for the organisation, drive initiatives at a programme level over the longer term, and be accountable for realising outcomes that advance ACRA's transformation goals. You will collaborate with senior leadership in defining strategy and ensuring its alignment to organisational needs, while serving as a trusted thought leader within the programme and with key stakeholders. Strategic Planning and Transformation You will support the CIO in shaping and executing ACRA's strategic IT direction, including the development and refresh of the Digital Transformation Plan. This includes translating ACRA's corporate goals into a coherent digital strategy, identifying opportunities to leverage technology for regulatory excellence, and driving the organisation's transition from project-based delivery to a product-led model. You will be expected to think across the full horizon, from immediate operational needs to longer-term capability building and ensure that ACRA's digital investments are purposeful, prioritised, and aligned to mission outcomes. Programme Delivery and Oversight You will oversee the delivery of ACRA's digital programme, spanning product development, system modernisation, and service transformation initiatives including AI. jobs.jd: Posting Date: 16 Apr 2026. GovTech is the lead agency driving Singapore’s Smart Nation initiatives and public sector digital transformation. As the Centre of Excellence for Infocomm Technology and Smart Systems (ICT & SS), GovTech develops the Singapore Government’s capabilities in Data Science & Artificial Intelligence, Application Development, Smart City Technology, Digital Infrastructure, and Cybersecurity. At GovTech, we offer you a purposeful career to make lives better where we empower our people to master their craft through robust learning and development opportunities all year round. Play a part in Singapore’s vision to build a Smart Nation and embark on your meaningful journey to build tech for public good. Join us to advance our mission and shape your future with us today! Learn more about GovTech at tech.gov.sg. [What you will be working on] GovTech builds the digital infrastructure behind Singapore's Smart Nation vision. The Data Programme is focused on one of the harder problems in that space: how analysts, engineers, and policymakers across government discover, access, and make sense of data that shapes real decisions. As a Director / Deputy Director, Design Management, you'd be the most senior design voice in the programme — setting direction, defining what good looks like, and building interaction models that don't really have a playbook yet. Lead discovery across the data ecosystem — uncovering where agencies get stuck accessing, understanding, and acting on government data Design interaction models that span the full stack: UI, APIs, CLI, and AI-driven interfaces, with coherence across all of them Define the principles and patterns for how data is surfaced, trusted, and used in high-stakes, sensitive environments Shape how the programme thinks about design — influencing product, engineering, and policy on what good looks like and why it matters Drive adoption of what gets built, treating usage and impact as design problems, not someone else's problem You'll thrive here if You think in systems and interaction paradigms, not just screens You're energised by problems that don't have established playbooks You hold a strong point of view and know how to bring senior stakeholders along with it You care as much about whether something gets used as whether it gets built [What we are looking for] 12+ years of experience, with a track record at principal level — shaping platforms, ecosystems, or systems-scale products i n multi-stakeholder environments Deep experience with data-heavy products: search, APIs, dashboards, or developer tooling Technical fluency — comfortable enough with APIs and data models to co-create with engineers, not just hand off to them A portfolio that shows paradigm-level thinking, not just execution; experience in AI-native interactions or regulated/public sector environments is a strong plus What you can expect A genuinely novel problem and the seniority to shape how it gets solved — this is not an execution role- Work with real consequences: the data infrastructure you help define underpins how government operates and makes decisions GovTech is an equal opportunity employer committed to fostering an inclusive workplace that values diverse voices and perspectives, as we believe it is key to innovation. Our employee benefits are based on a total rewards approach, offering a holistic and market-competitive suite of perks. We champion flexible work arrangements (subject to your job role) and trust you to manage your time to deliver your best. Learn more about life inside GovTech at go.gov.sg/GovTechCareers. jobs.title: Senior Manager/Assistant Director, Responsible AI & Governance AI Strategy Office (AISO)
jobs.jd: Posting Date: 12 Aug 2026. GovTech is the lead agency driving Singapore’s Smart Nation initiatives and public sector digital transformation. As the Centre of Excellence for Infocomm Technology and Smart Systems (ICT & SS), GovTech develops the Singapore Government’s capabilities in Data Science & Artificial Intelligence, Application Development, Smart City Technology, Digital Infrastructure, and Cybersecurity. At GovTech, we offer you a purposeful career to make lives better where we empower our people to master their craft through robust learning and development opportunities all year round. Play a part in Singapore’s vision to build a Smart Nation and embark on your meaningful journey to build tech for public good. Join us to advance our mission and shape your future with us today! Learn more about GovTech at tech.gov.sg. About the Role Artificial Intelligence presents significant opportunities for Government, but its adoption must be safe, responsible and trustworthy. As the Responsible AI & Governance Manager, you will help shape how GovTech governs AI adoption across the organisation. You will develop practical governance frameworks, operationalise AI policies, and partner with teams to ensure AI solutions are developed and deployed responsibly while enabling innovation. Rather than acting as a compliance gatekeeper, you will work closely with delivery teams to embed governance into the way AI products and services are designed, built and operated. What You Will Do Responsible AI Frameworks Develop and maintain GovTech's Responsible AI governance frameworks. Translate AI principles and policies into practical implementation guidance. Design governance artefacts, assessment methodologies and operational processes. Support teams in adopting responsible AI practices throughout the product lifecycle. AI Governance & Oversight Design and continuously improve governance processes for AI initiatives. Coordinate governance forums and decision-making mechanisms. Support governance reviews of higher-risk and higher-impact AI use cases. Develop governance playbooks, templates and operating procedures. Promote risk-based governance approaches that enable safe experimentation and innovation. AI Risk Management Identify emerging risks arising from AI technologies and adoption patterns. Develop practical approaches for assessing and managing AI-related risks. Coordinate AI incident reviews and lessons-learned processes. Track remediation actions and implementation of governance recommendations. Monitor governance effectiveness and propose improvements where necessary. Cross-functional Partnership Work closely with teams across: Product Engineering Cybersecurity Legal Procurement Data Governance Enterprise Architecture to ensure that governance expectations are practical, proportionate and aligned with delivery realities. Horizon Scanning & Policy Development Monitor developments in AI governance globally. Assess implications of emerging technologies, standards and regulations. Benchmark governance approaches across industry and government. Recommend updates to governance frameworks, policies and operating models. Who We're Looking For You enjoy solving difficult governance problems while enabling innovation. You understand that good governance should help organisations move faster and more confidently, rather than simply adding process and control. You are comfortable balancing competing priorities, exercising sound judgement under uncertainty, and working with multidisciplinary teams to solve novel challenges. You may come from backgrounds such as: Responsible AI Technology Governance Trust & Safety Technology Risk Cyber Governance Product Policy Digital Policy Data Governance AI Assurance Requirements Approximately 10 years of relevant experience. Strong judgement and structured thinking. Ability to balance innovation with risk management. Excellent stakeholder management and influencing skills. Strong written communication and policy
